title: Projection task records claim sourceAdapterVersion backlog-json/1 regardless of the backend that produced them
description:
Every projection task record is stamped `sourceAdapterVersion: "backlog-json/1"` as a HARD-CODED LITERAL (src/core/projection.ts, in the task-record loop), no matter which tracker backend actually produced it. A Quest-backed repository -- which is lore's DEFAULT for new bundles since commit 3c4c239 -- exports records claiming they came from Backlog.md.

Found while implementing LCLI-476 (dependency edges). Not fixed there deliberately: LCLI-476 was already changing the projection shape and its schema version, and folding an unrelated provenance correction into that change would have made both harder to review and harder to revert independently.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING COSMETIC. The field exists to tell a consumer WHERE a record came from, which is the one question it is unable to answer. It sits in the same record as the `dependencies` field LCLI-476 just added -- and that field's emptiness is backend-dependent (Quest's list carries dependencies, Backlog.md's and Jira's do not). So a consumer trying to distinguish "this task genuinely has no prerequisites" from "this backend does not report them" would reach for exactly this field, and be told Backlog.md in every case. The two defects compound: one field is silent about the backend, and another field's meaning depends on the backend.

That is this release's own theme pointed at our own projection: the record cannot express something a consumer needs, and unlike a missing field this one is worse -- it does not omit the answer, it states a wrong one. A silent contract is recoverable; a confidently incorrect one is not.

SHAPE OF A FIX, not prescribed: the adapter already knows what it is (`resolveSelectedBackend`, and each adapter has its own identity), so the value should be threaded from the producing adapter rather than literal at the projection site. Whoever takes it should decide whether the existing "backlog-json/1" string stays the value for the Backlog backend (probably yes -- retained projections carry it and provenance reads them) and what the Quest and Jira spellings are.

CHECK FOR THE CLASS, NOT THE INSTANCE. LCLI-476 found TWO other hard-coded literals of exactly this kind -- a projection schema version compared as "1.0" in ladybug-lifecycle, and a synthesized workspace manifest announcing "1.0" while emitting the current shape -- and added a source-scanning invariant test (test/projection.test.ts) that fails if a schema-version literal reappears outside projection.ts. Consider whether that invariant should be widened to cover adapter-identity literals too, rather than fixing this one site.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A projection produced against a Quest-backed repository stamps a value naming Quest, not `backlog-json/1`, and the same for Jira.
The value is threaded from the producing adapter rather than written as a literal at the projection site, so a new backend cannot be added without supplying one.
Whether `backlog-json/1` remains the Backlog backend`s value is decided explicitly and recorded, since retained projections already carry it and `lore provenance` reads those.
Retained projections produced before this change still load — the tolerant-read property LCLI-476 established must not regress.
Consideration is given to widening LCLI-476`s source-scanning invariant test to adapter-identity literals, and the decision either way is recorded rather than left implicit.
`bun run lint`, `typecheck` and the test suite pass, and `lore check` exits 0.
